name: chart
description: A chart under the answer, only when the user asks for a chart, graph or diagram. A log (a weight, a measurement): give its path as source and no points; the app reads and plots every entry itself, so do not cat it first and do not copy its values. A series a command prints as cat -t prints a log, such as the weather over the last days (weather --place=Göteborg --days=7, field temperature): give that command as line and no points; the app runs it and plots every row. Otherwise points, at most 60: numbers you counted from the results, or ones you worked out yourself, such as counts in a text the user gave.

kind.description: line for a value over time, bar to compare, pie for parts of one whole.

title.description: A short title, in the language of the reply.

unit.description: What the values are in: "kg", "bilder". A log's own unit is used when left out.

source.description: The path of a log to plot, every entry by its date.

line.description: A command line that prints the series, a line each as <time> TAB <JSON>, when there is no source: weather --place=Göteborg --days=7.

field.description: Which number of each entry to plot when it has several: temperature, windSpeed, windDirection or cloudCover for weather.

points.description: The values, in order, when there is no source.
